newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB seen at low 126, little impact from Deng.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB seen at low 126, little impact from Deng.

text.p: Key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures are likely to stay at the lower end of 126 yen on Thursday, with little impact from news of the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, traders said.
His death may have little impact on yen bonds because the dollar/yen rate stayed within the recent range, they said.

"The dollar/yen rate has been within the familiar range since his death, and the Tokyo stock market is likely to react little to the news," said Kazuto Uchida, a senior analyst at Tokyo Mitsubishi Securities. Dollar buying such as occurred at the time of the Tiananmen incident was unlikely, he said.

"The JGB market is unlikely to move unless the Hong Kong stock market reacts more drastically to Deng's death than it did in the last few days, when his weak health was reported," said Yasuhiro Motohashi, a senior bond trader at Tokai International Securities. "The dollar is unlikely to rise further against the yen as the current level is one where the market is cautious about dollar-selling intervention."

Traders said movement in JGB futures is likely to remain rang-bound on Thursday, although the key March contract may slip below a support point of 126.00 simply due to a correction after Wednesday's rise.
But others said short-covering before a shift in the benchmark, expected next week, was likely to keep providing a solid floor.
Another factor supporting the March contract is large-lot short positions built recently at around 126.10, because these positions are to be covered in the near future, traders said.
